segments.text: Let's start with a simple prompt.
What should I name my new dog?
When you submit a question like this, the AI calculates what those words mean together.
But that creates an immediate, mechanical problem.
How does a mathematical system determine the very first word of its response?
It solves this using a continuous feedback loop.
The AI relies on both your original question and whatever text it has already generated
as the context to predict what comes next.
To make the underlying math easier to see in this explanation,
we are going to simplify the model.
We'll treat whole words as individual tokens.
Before the AI can generate a single letter of a response,
it has to execute a precise, internal preparation sequence on your prompt.
This diagram maps out the four steps your question passes through
before inference actually begins.
In steps 1 and 2, the system breaks your sentence into individual token pieces,
and then assigns positional markers so it knows exactly where each piece sits in the sequence.
Step 3 converts each token into starting vectors.
These green bar charts represent arrays of numbers
that carry the baseline dictionary definition of each word.
Finally, in step 4, these numbers pass through a stack of transformation layers.
Here, attention mechanisms cross-reference the tokens,
updating their numerical values based on the surrounding text.
This pipeline takes a static human sentence
and converts it into a dynamic mathematical state.
The AI is now prepared to reason.
Track the final token, the question mark.
Moving through the layers,
its numerical vector updates exclusively using information from preceding tokens.
Exiting the final layer, its numbers completely change,
now mathematically describing an inquiry about naming a doc.
Look at this side-by-side comparison.
On the left, the question mark's vector reflects naming a dog.
On the right, following a prompt about cooking dinner,
the exact same symbol produces a vector reflecting choosing a meal.
In this system, identical symbols do not hold fixed definitions.
Their mathematical weight is dictated entirely by the history of the sequence they complete.
This brings us to the crucial handoff.
The AI takes the fully updated vector of that final input token,
the question mark, and uses it to predict the very first token of its answer.
At this exact millisecond, the generated reply has no tokens yet.
The system calculates the probability of thousands of potential starting words.
This interface displays the top predictions.
U holds the highest probability at 18 percent, A sits at 14 percent, and Great at 9 percent,
with all other tokens combined making up 59 percent.
The system selects U, highlighting it and adding it to the beginning of the reply.
U immediately becomes the new final token.
Its updated vector now contains the context of your original question
plus the single word of the reply, and those numbers are used to predict the next step.
Generating a single word creates a brand new context window,
perpetually driving the system forward to the next calculation.
The AI repeats the cycle rapidly, adding could, name, him, strictly one token at a time.
Each new token is locked in as a permanent part of the context,
continually shifting the underlying mathematics of the sequence.
With the context now reading, you could name him,
the mathematical probabilities heavily skew toward outputting a dog's name.
Checking the prediction spread again, spot takes a clear lead at 22 percent.
Max follows at 17 percent, and Buddy at 14.
The AI selects spot in this instance.
But because this is a probabilistic system, running the exact same prompt a second time
could lead the AI to select a completely different name from the list.
AI responses are never retrieved intact from a hidden database.
They are grown organically, built on a chain of calculated probabilities.
After completing the sentence, you could name him spot,
the system predicts and adds a period.
It doesn't stop there by accident.
It calculates one final step, predicting a specialized, invisible, end-of-answer token.
This symbol acts as a hard stop condition.
It signals to the system that the reply is complete, terminating the predictive loop.
As this banner states, every single generated answer
is constructed through this precise method, one token at a time.
This entire cycle, from translating text into math,
predicting probabilities, and reaching the final stop token, is called inference.
